newsitem.title: USA: Fruit of the Loom sees improved oper profit.
newsitem.headline: Fruit of the Loom sees improved oper profit.

text.p: Fruit of the Loom Inc said Wednesday that it expects an improved operating performance in 1997.

"With a wealth of new sales and marketing talent onboard, we will bring to market a number of new products across all our product lines," Richard Lappin, president, said in a statement. "To support these new products we have an aggressive advertising and promotional campaign in excess of $130 million with an emphasis on the Gitano, Pro Player and the Fruit of the Loom brands."
Lappin added that the company has invested heavily in improved product quality and in customer service.

"Our highly successful VMI (vendor managed inventory) service has allowed us to partner with our customers to help reduce their working capital needs while allowing us to more accurately forecast sales trends," he said.
He said the comapny continues to improve productivity and cut costs, offsetting the effects of a continued competitive pricing environment for basic family apparel.
"All of this should lead to improved operating performance in 1997 and increased shareholder returns," Lappin said.
Fruit of the Loom makes basic apparel, including underwear, activewear, casual clothing, sportswear and clothing for children.

Earlier, the company reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.56 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $4.05 a share after a $158.5 million writedown of goodwill. Sales rose to $581.0 million from $508.8 million, an increase of 14 percent.

Revenue growth in the quarter reflected strong shipments of blank t-shirts, casualwear fleece products, women's and girls' underwear and Gitano jeans, the company said. International operations were up 11 percent in the quarter.

"Profitability improved due to benefits derived from our offshore sewing operations," William Farley, chairman, said in a statement. "There is every reason to believe that this positive momentum will carry over into 1997 operations."
